label: Seed & Germination
learningGoals: Distinguish the achene fruit wall from the true seed and embryo tissues
Separate seed viability questions from environmental failure patterns

lessons.title: Seed anatomy
lessons.summary: Distinguish the whole cannabis achene from the true seed and locate the pericarp, seed coat, residual peripheral endosperm, cotyledons, radicle, hypocotyl region, and plumule.

lessons.title: Imbibition
lessons.summary: See how water uptake rehydrates seed tissues and restarts metabolic activity before visible germination.

lessons.title: Radicle emergence
lessons.summary: Follow the radicle as the first root organ emerges and establishes the direction of early seedling growth.

lessons.title: Cotyledon transition
lessons.summary: Track emergence from the seed shell through cotyledon opening and the first true leaves.

lessons.title: Germination failure patterns
lessons.summary: Compare stalled seeds, damping-off risk, shell retention, excessive moisture, and temperature-related delays without assuming one cause from appearance alone.

lessons.title: Reserve mobilization
lessons.summary: Follow stored lipids, proteins, and other seed reserves as germination restarts metabolism and supports embryo growth before expanding leaves become the dominant current carbon source.
lessons.visual: Seed reserve mobilization cutaway and flow map

label: Root System
learningGoals: Distinguish primary, lateral, and fine absorbing roots
Understand root hairs and rhizosphere exchange
Connect root oxygen and water status to whole-plant behavior

lessons.title: Root architecture
lessons.summary: Follow primary roots, lateral branching, fine roots, and root hairs through the occupied media volume.

lessons.title: Root hairs & absorption
lessons.summary: See where most short-lived absorbing surface develops and how root hairs increase contact with the surrounding solution and media.

lessons.title: Rhizosphere
lessons.summary: Explore the narrow root-influenced zone where water, ions, microbes, exudates, and oxygen conditions interact.

lessons.title: Water & nutrient uptake
lessons.summary: Connect substrate moisture, ion availability, root membrane transport, transpiration demand, and vascular movement.

lessons.title: Root stress
lessons.summary: Compare low oxygen, persistent saturation, excessive dryback, salt stress, temperature stress, and visible root decline as patterns that require context.

lessons.title: Root-zone oxygen diffusion
lessons.summary: Compare air-filled and water-filled pore space to understand why oxygen replenishment can become limiting when media remains saturated and root or microbial respiration continues.

label: Stem & Vascular System
learningGoals: Connect training damage to vascular recovery

lessons.title: Stem cross-section
lessons.summary: Identify epidermal, cortex, vascular, and pith regions in a simplified cannabis stem cross-section.

lessons.title: Xylem transport
lessons.summary: Follow water and dissolved mineral movement from roots toward transpiring shoots and leaves.

lessons.title: Phloem transport
lessons.summary: Follow movement of photosynthate from source tissues toward growing and storage sinks throughout the plant.

lessons.title: Internodal spacing
lessons.summary: Connect internode length to developmental stage, genetics, light environment, temperature, and growth rate rather than treating it as a single-variable trait.

lessons.title: Damage & recovery
lessons.summary: See how bending, crushing, pruning, and breakage affect support and transport and why damage severity matters.

lessons.title: Source-sink integration
lessons.summary: Connect mature exporting leaves with changing sinks such as expanding shoots, roots, flowers, and developing seeds to understand how phloem allocation shifts through development.

label: Nodes & Branching
learningGoals: Locate nodes, internodes, and axillary buds

lessons.title: Node anatomy
lessons.summary: Locate the leaf attachment, axillary bud, branch origin, and adjoining internodes at a cannabis node.

lessons.title: Apical dominance
lessons.summary: Understand how the shoot apex influences lateral growth and why removing or repositioning the apex changes branching behavior.

lessons.title: Topping & FIM
lessons.summary: Compare removal points and the resulting redistribution of active shoot growth without treating every plant response as identical.

lessons.title: LST & directional growth
lessons.summary: See how branch orientation and light exposure can redistribute canopy height while preserving tissue continuity.

lessons.title: Mainlining & SCROG
lessons.summary: Compare structured branch selection with screen-based canopy distribution as different ways to organize growing points.

lessons.title: Branch angle & mechanical support
lessons.summary: Treat branches as loaded structures by connecting attachment angle, diameter, leverage, tissue condition, supported mass, movement, and external support instead of using angle alone as a strength score.
lessons.visual: Branch load and support force diagram

label: Leaves
learningGoals: Use a healthy leaf as the diagnostic baseline

lessons.title: Healthy leaf baseline
lessons.summary: Use leaflet shape, venation, petiole, surface condition, color distribution, and posture as the reference before judging abnormality.

lessons.title: Photosynthesis
lessons.summary: Connect light capture, carbon dioxide entry, water status, chloroplast function, and carbohydrate production.

lessons.title: Stomata & transpiration
lessons.summary: Link stomatal opening, vapor pressure conditions, carbon dioxide exchange, and water loss.

lessons.title: Symptom pattern language
lessons.summary: Describe chlorosis, necrosis, spotting, curl, wilt, and texture by location and distribution before assigning a cause.

lessons.title: Leaf inspection workflow
lessons.summary: Inspect upper and lower surfaces, new and old growth, margins, veins, petioles, pests, residue, and progression over time.

lessons.title: Leaf temperature & energy balance
lessons.summary: See how absorbed radiation, convective exchange, airflow, stomatal behavior, and evaporative cooling can make leaf temperature differ from surrounding air temperature.

label: Flowers
learningGoals: Use multiple maturity signals instead of one visual cue

lessons.title: Female flower anatomy
lessons.summary: Locate bracts, stigmas, pistillate structures, sugar leaves, and dense floral clusters using a labeled reference.

lessons.title: Flower initiation
lessons.summary: Follow the transition from preflower expression into expanding floral sites and stacked inflorescences.

lessons.title: Bud development
lessons.summary: Track changes in bract expansion, stigma appearance, resin coverage, density, and senescence across maturation.

lessons.title: Pollination response
lessons.summary: See how successful pollination redirects development toward seed formation and changes the appearance of individual floral structures.

lessons.title: Maturity & risk inspection
lessons.summary: Combine trichome condition, flower development, senescence, cultivar behavior, and mold inspection rather than relying on stigma color alone.

lessons.title: Photoperiod sensing & floral transition
lessons.summary: Separate the plant's response to day and night length from the later appearance of visible flowers by following signaling, shoot-apex change, internode response, and progressive inflorescence development.
lessons.visual: Photoperiod signal to visible flower transition timeline

label: Trichomes & Resin
learningGoals: Identify the resin head and stalk

lessons.title: Trichome types
lessons.summary: Compare capitate-stalked, capitate-sessile, and bulbous glandular trichome forms by scale and structure.

lessons.title: Gland anatomy
lessons.summary: Identify the stalk, gland head, secretory region, and cuticular storage space in a simplified glandular trichome model.

lessons.title: Where to inspect
lessons.summary: Compare trichomes on bracts and nearby sugar leaves and avoid treating every visible gland as equally representative of floral maturity.

lessons.title: Clear, cloudy & amber
lessons.summary: Use apparent optical condition as one observation among several, recognizing that lighting, focus, tissue sampled, and cultivar can affect interpretation.

lessons.title: Microscope workflow
lessons.summary: Standardize magnification, sample location, lighting, and repeated observations so maturity comparisons are more consistent.

lessons.title: Secretory disk & storage cavity
lessons.summary: Zoom into the gland head to connect secretory disk cells, the expanding cuticle, and the subcuticular cavity where secreted resin accumulates.
lessons.visual: Gland-head secretory disk and storage-cavity cutaway

label: Sex, Pollen & Seeds
learningGoals: Distinguish common male and female reproductive structures

lessons.title: Male vs female preflowers
lessons.summary: Compare developing staminate and pistillate structures at nodes using multiple views and developmental stages.

lessons.title: Mixed-sex expression
lessons.summary: Identify anthers or staminate structures appearing on otherwise female plants and distinguish observations from assumptions about cause.

lessons.title: Pollen biology
lessons.summary: Follow pollen production, release, transport, stigma contact, and the first steps toward fertilization.

lessons.title: Seed formation
lessons.summary: Track ovule fertilization through developing seed coat, embryo, filling, and physical maturity.

lessons.title: Controlled pollination
lessons.summary: Map isolation, pollen handling, target selection, labeling, and record keeping as the core observational workflow for intentional crosses.

lessons.title: Fertilization & seed filling
lessons.summary: Separate pollen arrival from successful fertilization, then follow embryo development, reserve accumulation, seed-coat maturation, and the progression toward physical seed maturity.
lessons.visual: Pollen contact to embryo and seed-filling sequence

label: Environment Overlay
learningGoals: Connect leaf and root responses to atmospheric demand
Relate light and temperature to transpiration
Use measurements as context instead of isolated targets

lessons.title: Light distribution
lessons.summary: Map high- and low-light zones across the canopy and connect PPFD distribution to leaf position and canopy architecture.

lessons.title: Temperature & humidity
lessons.summary: See how air temperature and relative humidity combine to shape evaporative demand rather than acting as independent numbers.

lessons.title: VPD & transpiration
lessons.summary: Connect vapor pressure deficit to stomatal behavior, leaf temperature, water movement, and changing plant demand.

lessons.title: Airflow & boundary layer
lessons.summary: Visualize air movement around leaves and the still-air boundary layer that influences heat and vapor exchange.

lessons.title: Root-zone interaction
lessons.summary: Overlay media moisture, oxygen, pH, EC, root temperature, and atmospheric demand to show why plant response depends on the whole system.

lessons.title: Leaf temperature vs air temperature
lessons.summary: Compare measured leaf and air temperatures and connect their difference to radiation, airflow, transpiration, humidity, and the vapor-pressure gradient at the leaf surface.

label: Diagnostic Overlay
learningGoals: Use old-vs-new and upper-vs-lower growth patterns
Build a differential rather than a single visual guess

lessons.title: Symptom location
lessons.summary: Mark whether the first visible problem begins on old leaves, new growth, upper canopy, lower canopy, one branch, roots, or the whole plant.

lessons.title: Pattern description
lessons.summary: Describe uniform, interveinal, marginal, spotted, tip-focused, twisted, wilted, or asymmetric symptoms before assigning cause.

lessons.title: Progression over time
lessons.summary: Compare sudden, gradual, stable, spreading, and recovering patterns and record what changed before symptoms appeared.

lessons.title: Measurement context
lessons.summary: Bring pH, EC, substrate moisture, temperature, RH, VPD, PPFD, and feed/water history into the same diagnostic record.

lessons.title: Differential workflow
lessons.summary: Rank plausible environmental, root-zone, nutritional, pest, pathogen, and physical explanations and use new observations to narrow them.

lessons.title: Genotype × environment context
lessons.summary: Use cultivar baselines, repeatability, developmental stage, environment, and plant-to-plant comparison to distinguish a stable phenotype from a newly emerging stress or disease pattern.
